Operator: Good day, and welcome to the AstraNet Communications Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the presentation portion of the call. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to AstraNet Communications' Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Network Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Commercial Officer; David Lee, Chief Technology Officer; Karen Wong, Chief Operating Officer; and other members of our leadership team. Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3, demonstrating our continued commitment to growth and innovation. Our success is driven by our dedicated team and strategic investments. Our key achievements include robust EBITDA margin expansion reflecting operational leverage in our integrated telecom and media operations, even amid heavy next-gen infrastructure spending. The launches of AstraStream Ultra, 5G Flex Home, and EdgeMedia Pro are exceeding expectations, driving $285 million in incremental revenue and 1.2 million net subscriber adds. Further milestones encompass strong free cash flow generation that supports shareholder returns and growth bets. We are also focusing on ARPU uplift through targeted pricing and bundling. Our dedication to cost discipline in revenue costs is bearing fruit, with efficiencies offsetting data growth pressures. Our strategy is to enhance subscriber growth with clear guidance ahead. We are actively investing in lowering subscriber acquisition costs via data-driven tactics. We are also exploring spectrum optimization and finally, analyzing sustained network utilization for premium services.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Sarah. Now, let's review our financial performance. Revenue for the quarter reached $35.7 billion, reflecting a 12% increase year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA was $13.7 billion, resulting in a margin of 38.5%, up 230 basis points from 36.2% in Q3 2022 and our strongest quarterly margin in five years. On a full-year basis through Q3, we're at 37.8%, on track for the top end of our 37-39% guidance for fiscal 2023. We maintain a disciplined approach to cost management and capital allocation. Capital expenditures totaled $7.8 billion, primarily allocated to expanding our 5G network, fiber infrastructure, and content investments.

Turning deeper into our EBITDA margin performance, this expansion stems from operational leverage across our wireless, broadband, and media segments. Wireless was the standout, driving over 60% of the uplift, with postpaid ARPU at $52.30, up 4.2% year-over-year, thanks to our 5G Standalone rollout covering 85% of top 100 markets and 15% higher data usage from UHD streaming and cloud gaming. Smartphone upgrades with iPhone 15 and Galaxy S24 pushed 5G penetration to 62% of our 45 million postpaid base. Fixed Wireless Access added 750,000 net adds with margins over 50%, leveraging our 2.5 GHz spectrum to challenge cable players like Comcast.

In broadband, Fiber-to-the-Home revenue grew 22% to $2.8 billion, margins up 450 basis points to 42%, as we passed 18 million homes, with 38% conversion via automated provisioning and AI planning, cutting CapEx per home to $850. Legacy copper migration added 150 basis points. On media, WaveStream hit 28 million paid users, ad-tier ARPU up 12% to $9.50, offset by bundling our TeleMedia Bundle at 40% penetration, holding media margins steady at 25%.

Headwinds like regulatory pressures in Europe—where our Vodafone JV contributes 12% of revenue—shaved 100 basis points, with EU roaming caps up 5%, but Nokia edge partnerships generated $250 million in high-margin revenue. U.S. spectrum amortization rose $150 million quarter-over-quarter but is front-loaded for 90% 3.7 GHz coverage. SG&A fell 210 basis points to 18% via zero-based budgeting and BPO, with Open RAN trials cutting opex 7% per site, targeting 20% RAN by 2025. North America drove 75% of expansion at 40.1% margins, post our regional cable acquisition synergies of $400 million. APAC at 28%, Latin America at 32% amid FX.

We anticipate 200-300 basis points annual expansion through 2025 from 5G-Advanced, enterprise networks targeting $1.5 billion, and FAST channels.

On new product launches, these are pivotal: AstraStream Ultra bundles linear TV, FAST, and AI recs with Netflix integrations at $25 standalone or $15 bundled, adding $95 million revenue and 130k subs, with U.S. at 70% of adds. 5G Flex Home FWA delivered $120 million and 420k households at 1Gbps via n78 and mmWave. EdgeMedia Pro secured $40 million Q2 bookings from ESPN pilots. Total: $285 million revenue, 1.2 million adds, blended ARPU to $58.75. We project $1.1 billion full-year incremental, gaining 150 basis points U.S. wireless share.

Free cash flow hit $3.2 billion, up 18% year-over-year, TTM $12.5 billion at 14% yield. Operating cash $4.8 billion from wireless $8.1 billion up 7% and broadband $4.2 billion up 9%. Capex at 22% of revenue, optimized via Open RAN. Utilization: shareholder returns $6.9 billion (55%), including $4.2 billion buybacks and $2.7 billion dividends up 8%; debt reduction $3.1 billion to 2.3x leverage; growth $1.9 billion in RAN, content, edge AI; flexibility $600 million for M&A like Mexican fiber.

ARPU trends show blended $58.40, up 4.8% or $2.65 year-over-year. Postpaid mobile $49.20 up 3.7% from pricing hikes and 28% premium 5G tiers. Broadband $68.75 up 6.2% from FTTH premiums. Video/streaming $42.10 up 5.1% via TeleMedia Ultimate Bundle at $145, 62% quad-play penetration. Pricing 60% of lift, bundling 40%, with North America +5.5%, Europe +2.1%, LatAm +6.8%. Guide 4.5-5.0% FY24.

Cost of revenue at $12.8 billion, up 4.2% but 44.8% of revenue, down 80 basis points. Wireless $7.1 billion up 6.8% from 18% data growth, offset by $320 million Open RAN savings. Broadband $3.9 billion up 2.1%, virtualization savings $180 million. Media $1.8 billion flat via content deals. North America $10.9 billion up 4.5%, Europe $1.3 billion up 3.2%. Efficiencies saved $650 million via AI energy cuts. Q4 guide $13.0-13.3 billion.

For guidance, Q4 RGUs +2.8-3.2% or 1.1-1.3 million adds: wireless 750-850k, broadband 250-300k, streaming 100-150k. FY25 RGUs +4.5-5.5% or 4.8-5.6 million. Q4 revenue $28.4-28.9 billion +3-5%; FY25 $113.5-116.0 billion +4-6.5%.

SAC averaged $415, down 9% year-over-year. Wireless $408 down 8%, broadband $575 down 7%, streaming $62 down 14% via digital ads. U.S. $390 down 11%, LatAm/APAC $320 down 16%. SAC/LTV 1:10.2, Q3 $410-420.

Finally, spectrum utilization at 78%, low-band 85%, mid-band 82% at 4.2 bits/Hz, mmWave 62% for enterprise. Refarming 3G to 5G, CBRS pursuits, O-RAN pilots for 90% utilization.

Mike Chen: Thank you. I'm pleased to provide an update on our network advancements. We've significantly expanded our 5G coverage to 95% nationwide, delivering faster speeds and lower latency. Our network reliability remains high at 99.99%, and we are continuously optimizing our infrastructure to meet growing demand, including Open RAN scaling to 20% by 2025. We are also focusing on enhancing our cybersecurity posture with AI-driven threat detection. We are committed to spectrum-efficient deployments that support FWA and edge services for media.

Lisa Patel: Thank you. I'm excited to share our commercial achievements. We've seen strong subscriber growth of 1.2 million net adds across services, outpacing peers. Customer satisfaction remains a top priority, with NPS over 55, and we are continuously improving the customer experience through AI personalization. We are also focused on expanding our partnerships, like Disney and Paramount, to offer bundled services and enhance customer value. We are prioritizing low SAC through omnichannel acquisition and bundling uptake.

David Lee: Thank you. From a technology perspective, we are focused on driving innovation and leveraging emerging technologies to transform our business. We are exploring the use of AI and machine learning to automate network operations, improve customer service via CDP processing 10 petabytes daily, and develop new products like network slicing for 8K streaming. We are also investing in research and development, including 6G testbeds, to stay ahead of the curve. Our technological direction is converged edge-cloud for AR/VR and private networks.

Karen Wong: Thank you. Operationally, we are focused on improving efficiency and streamlining our processes with zero-based budgeting and predictive maintenance. We are leveraging data analytics to optimize our resource allocation and improve decision-making, targeting 200 basis points cost leverage. We are also committed to sustainability, reducing energy 17% across sites. Our operational focus is Network 2.0 automation for zero-touch ops.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your content strategy and your plans for investing in original programming, and what is the anticipated impact on subscriber growth?

Sarah Thompson: Thanks, Emily. Our content strategy centers on originals co-produced with Lionsgate and sports rights like NBA regionals, amortized efficiently at $450 million quarterly. We're investing $600 million annually in WaveStream+, bundling with wireless for 40% penetration, driving 2.1 million adds to 28 million paid users and $250 million ARPU uplift. This reverses cord-cutting, targeting 10-12% media growth FY25 with churn under 2%.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Kim: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your plans for addressing the digital divide and ensuring that all communities have access to affordable broadband, and how do you plan to achieve 22% penetration in eligible FWA areas?

Lisa Patel: Great question, David. We're tackling the digital divide via 5G Flex Home FWA in rural Midwest and Southeast, adding 420k households at $85 ARPU, hitting 22% penetration in 60 days post-launch. Combined with FTTH passing 18 million homes at 38% conversion, and Spectrum Rural CBRS partnerships, we're reducing backlog 15% while keeping SAC low through self-installs.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Lopez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Rachel Lopez: Can you discuss your capital allocation priorities and your plans for returning capital to shareholders, including free cash flow utilization?

John Ramirez: Absolutely, Rachel. FCF TTM $12.5 billion prioritizes returns at 55%—$4.2 billion buybacks at $48 average, $2.7 billion dividends up 8% to 4.8% yield—then delever to 2.3x, growth capex like $800 million Open RAN, and M&A dry powder. FY25 FCF $15-16 billion supports this balanced approach.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Hale with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Tom Hale: What are your strategies for navigating the changing regulatory landscape?

Sarah Thompson: Thanks, Tom. We're proactive on regs like FCC auctions, EU Gigabit Act, and net neutrality. Refarming legacy spectrum, filing 6G testbeds, and JVs like Vodafone offset roaming caps. Our 220 MHz mid-band moat and compliance via slicing ensure resilience, as seen in Ofcom wins.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Sarah, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Sarah Thompson: Thank you. In conclusion, we are pleased with our performance this quarter and remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and sustainability. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
